commitments.statement: On macOS, Browser MCP selects stable Microsoft Edge with one fixed per-user OwlBear-owned persistent profile and never reads, copies, or controls the operator's daily Edge profile.
Missing Edge, invalid mode, unusable Edge, or profile contention produces bounded unavailable state and never silently substitutes Chromium for the managed authentication path.
B1 first-use sign-in, site trust, consent, or MFA occurs directly in the visible lifespan-owned Edge window without B1 sending session material through an agent or MCP tool.

Browser readiness describes configured mechanics and process state, while authenticated success remains evidence for one target acquisition at one time and never becomes a universal authenticated claim.
Bundled Chromium remains explicitly selectable and non-macOS defaults remain unchanged; CDP attachment and daily-profile reuse are excluded from this Change.

commitments.provenance: observed pilot and existing package ownership
commitments.statement: Managed Edge uses supported sandbox configuration, integrates with the maintained exception-safe cleanup boundary, and is accepted through deterministic tests plus a bounded managed-device pilot.

acceptance: Given macOS with omitted BROWSER_MODE and stable Edge installed, Browser MCP launches the msedge channel with Chromium sandboxing and the fixed per-user OwlBear profile.
Given explicit BROWSER_MODE=chromium or a non-macOS host with omitted mode, Browser MCP launches the preserved Chromium mode and does not use the managed Edge profile.

Given missing Edge, invalid mode, the per-user Edge profile owned by another workspace, or another startup failure, Browser MCP reports edge-unavailable, invalid-mode, profile-in-use, or startup-failed respectively and does not launch Chromium as a substitute.

Given first use, the operator can complete sign-in, site trust, consent, or MFA directly in the visible lifespan-owned Edge window without B1 sending session material through an OwlBear request or result.

Given ready managed Edge, browser_status returns managed-edge, per-user-owned, ready, null startup reason, visible authentication available, null startup diagnostic, and no global authenticated field.
Given unavailable managed Edge, browser_status returns unavailable with its bounded reason and diagnostic and exposes no profile path, URL, hostname, page content, cookie, token, or session value.

Given no completed acquisition, browser_status returns null latest acquisition status; given one completed acquire call, it returns that AcquisitionStatus for this process without a persisted authentication claim.
Given the registered Browser MCP inventory and knowledge-ingestor definition, browser_status is read-only, idempotent, non-destructive, and granted beside acquire.

Given the managed-Mac pilot procedure, the lifespan-owned Edge page opens approved SharePoint and Jira targets with operator-confirmed authenticated content, retains session availability after profile restart, emits no rejected no-sandbox warning, and closes only OwlBear-owned resources.

Given the maintained Browser, Browser MCP, setup, seed, agent, and validation surfaces named in SCOPE-001, focused and routed checks pass without weakening #234 cleanup or claiming B2 target classification.
outcomes.promise: macOS Browser MCP provides one isolated authenticated Edge session and truthful readiness for its maintained ingestion caller without touching the daily browser or implying universal authentication.
outcomes.title: Managed Edge authentication readiness

acceptance_observations: AC-001: Given resolved managed-edge settings for ~/.owlbear/edge-profile, PlaywrightLauncher.launch passes channel=msedge, chromium_sandbox=True, headless=False, and that owned profile to the Playwright persistent-context boundary.

AC-002: Given managed-edge settings with extension-related environment values present, launcher startup does not discover/load the SSO extension or access the daily browser profile; given Chromium settings, the existing distinct profile and Chromium launch path remain usable.

AC-003: Given missing Edge, a contended owned profile, or another launch failure below PlaywrightLauncher.launch, the launcher exposes a classifiable failure and makes no substitute Chromium launch; closing after failure releases its owned resources.

AC-004: Given launch and then close, the public capability projection describes mode and persistent/visible mechanics without microsoft_sso or a global authenticated claim, then clears persistent/visible availability on close.

AC-005: Given a fetcher, context, or Playwright cleanup error/cancellation, the maintained launcher lifecycle tests still observe attempts for fetcher, context, and Playwright, detached handles, preserved control-flow exceptions, and no repeated cleanup on a second close.
constraints: Primary domain: browser. The MCP test-file edit is limited to tests of core launcher behavior; no MCP runtime change in this task.
Accept explicit resolved configuration from composition; retain existing SSO_EXTENSION_PATH/LOCALAPPDATA behavior only as needed for preserved non-macOS Chromium, never for macOS managed Edge.
Preserve explicit Chromium and the core Chromium default used by temporary headless acquisition fixtures; macOS default selection belongs to MCP composition in TASK-002.
Integrate through the existing #234 close/partial-startup boundary; retain cancellation propagation, independent resource cleanup, and idempotence.
No dependency-resolution input changes or new package are needed; do not introduce lockfile churn.
exclusions: Environment-driven macOS default selection or MCP status registration
Daily Edge profile access, copying, CDP attachment, automatic Chromium fallback
Target/page classification, generic interactive-tool changes, cleanup redesign
maintained_surfaces: serve/browser-mcp/tests/test_lifecycle.py (existing core launcher capability/cleanup assertions only)
proof_boundaries: Exercise PlaywrightLauncher.launch/page/capabilities/close with Playwright dependencies replaced below the public launcher; assert persistent-context call arguments and failure/no-fallback observations, not private helper output alone.

From the managed worktree, run uv run pytest serve/browser/tests/test_playwright_launcher.py serve/browser-mcp/tests/test_lifecycle.py -q --tb=short; run uv run test --changed for impacted consumers and invariants at the reviewed candidate.
This task proves launch mechanics and preserved cleanup, not enterprise authentication or target classification; real managed-device proof is required by TASK-004.
required_outputs: Typed resolved mode/profile inputs on PlaywrightLauncher; managed-edge uses stable msedge, chromium_sandbox=True, and the per-user OwlBear Edge profile supplied by composition without consulting daily-profile or extension settings.

Bounded launcher failure signals for missing Edge and profile contention, with other launch failures propagated for MCP startup-failed classification; no alternate browser launch after managed Edge failure.

Capability and public-export updates replacing microsoft_sso with mode, owned persistent-profile availability, and visible manual-authentication mechanics; focused launcher tests and adaptation of the existing core capability assertions in the MCP lifecycle test file.
tasks.result: The Browser core launches the selected owned persistent browser with truthful mechanical capabilities, typed fail-closed errors, and preserved cleanup and Chromium behavior.
tasks.title: Implement isolated managed Edge launcher mechanics

acceptance_observations: AC-006: Given macOS with omitted BROWSER_MODE and an arbitrary PLAYWRIGHT_USER_DATA_DIR, the assembled app_lifespan launches visible managed Edge at ~/.owlbear/edge-profile; given explicit chromium or non-macOS omission, it launches Chromium using the existing profile override/default and never the managed Edge profile.

AC-007: Given a ready managed Edge lifespan with its retained page, registered browser_status returns browser_mode=managed-edge, ownership=per-user-owned, startup_state=ready, startup_reason=null, visible_authentication=available, latest_acquisition_status=null, startup_diagnostic=null.

AC-008: Given missing Edge, invalid mode, profile contention, or another startup/page failure, registered browser_status reports startup_state=unavailable, visible_authentication=unavailable and respectively edge-unavailable, invalid-mode, profile-in-use, or startup-failed with a bounded diagnostic; invalid mode launches no browser and managed Edge failures launch no Chromium substitute.

AC-009: Given startup exceptions containing a profile path, URL, hostname, page text, cookie, token, or session sentinel, browser_status serialization exposes none of those values and contains only the seven canonical keys, with no authenticated field.

AC-010: Given no completed acquire, status reports null; after completed success or an AcquisitionFailure it reports that result's AcquisitionStatus; an in-flight or raised acquire does not invent a new status, and a fresh lifespan resets the value to null.

AC-011: Given Client(mcp).list_tools(), browser_status is present with readOnlyHint=true, idempotentHint=true, destructiveHint=false and the canonical output schema; invoking it through Client(mcp) does not call launch again, navigate, or acquire.

AC-012: Given lifespan startup/page failure, shutdown cleanup failure, or cancellation, the maintained lifecycle suite still observes page/launcher cleanup, cleared AppContext handles, and preserved cancellation behavior; ready managed startup retains the page until shutdown for direct operator interaction.
constraints: Primary domain: browser-mcp. Reuse AppContext, app_lifespan and _close_browser_resources; ordinary startup failure yields a diagnosable unavailable server, while cancellation/control-flow failures retain their cleanup and propagation behavior.

Canonical status keys: browser_mode, ownership, startup_state, startup_reason, visible_authentication, latest_acquisition_status, startup_diagnostic. browser_mode uses managed-edge|chromium; ownership is per-user-owned; startup_state is ready|unavailable; visible_authentication is available|unavailable.

startup_reason uses edge-unavailable|profile-in-use|invalid-mode|startup-failed|null. Construct bounded safe diagnostics at composition from typed/bounded launcher classification, never return raw exception text, profile paths, URLs, hostnames, content, cookies, tokens, or session values.
Keep acquire destination checks and AcquisitionStatus semantics intact; browser_status must not navigate, acquire, authenticate, inspect page content, or persist status.
Only the operator interacts directly with the lifespan-owned visible Edge page for sign-in, consent, site trust, or MFA; no B1 interactive MCP call or session-material transport.
exclusions: Universal or persisted authentication status, identity-integration claims
B2 target/readiness classification, B5 generic interactive-tool safety, SSRF/allowlist policy changes
Daily profile reuse, CDP, alternate-browser fallback, second cleanup framework
maintained_surfaces: serve/browser-mcp/src/owlbear_browser_mcp/__init__.py (public exports if required by existing convention)
serve/browser-mcp/tests/test_lifecycle.py (MCP startup/configuration/status and existing cleanup coverage)
proof_boundaries: Run the normal MCP lifespan and registered Client(mcp) list_tools/call_tool boundaries, replacing Playwright/browser dependencies below them so tests cannot use a real personal profile; test environment resolution through app_lifespan rather than a replacement completed context alone.

Run uv run pytest serve/browser-mcp/tests/test_lifecycle.py serve/browser-mcp/tests/test_acquire.py -q --tb=short from the managed worktree; provision the existing Chromium browser-marked fixture prerequisite or report it as unverified, never claim a skipped fixture passed.

Run uv run test --changed on the reviewed candidate for importing consumers and invariants; tests demonstrate process readiness and status dataflow, not B2 acquisition classification or managed-enterprise authentication.
required_outputs: Startup BROWSER_MODE resolution in app_lifespan: macOS omission selects managed-edge at fixed ~/.owlbear/edge-profile; explicit chromium and non-macOS omission preserve Chromium profile resolution; managed mode ignores PLAYWRIGHT_USER_DATA_DIR.
Read-only browser_status tool and public export using the seven canonical Design fields, safe bounded unavailable reasons/diagnostics, and no authentication claim or sensitive browser data.

Process-local latest_acquisition_status updated after acquire completes with an AcquisitionStatus; retained lifespan page for direct manual onboarding; focused registered-tool, startup/configuration, acquisition-state, and lifecycle tests.
tasks.result: Browser MCP resolves platform-specific mode and profile settings, retains the visible owned page, exposes safe ready/unavailable status, and records only the latest completed acquisition status for this process.
tasks.title: Compose mode selection and process-local Browser status

acceptance_observations: AC-013: Given the maintained knowledge-ingestor definition and live Browser MCP registry, agent validation observes owlbear-browser/acquire and owlbear-browser/browser_status grants and resolves both to registered tools.

AC-014: Given the updated knowledge-ingestor instructions, artifact inspection finds that browser_status is limited to diagnosis/routing and cannot authorize ingestion or establish authenticated content; first-use interaction is assigned to the operator in the owned window without new interactive-tool grants.
constraints: Primary domain: agent-config. Preserve existing grants and the shared loading model; status routes to direct operator onboarding when needed without transporting secrets or invoking interactive MCP tools.
Depend on TASK-002 so the grant never references a missing registered tool at this task boundary.
Do not change knowledge ingestion authorization, replacement behavior, acquisition outcome meaning, or shared workflow authority.
exclusions: Knowledge runtime changes or B2/B5 implementation
New agent, new workflow, broad tool grants, session-material requests
proof_boundaries: Run uv run pytest tests/test_agent_ecosystem_validation.py tests/test_knowledge_ops_contract.py -q --tb=short from the reviewed worktree; the existing live-registry check and the added required-grant assertion must fail if registration or the caller grant is removed.
Inspect the narrow agent diff against its existing grants and the admitted Browser Status/First-Use contracts; run scoped repository agent validation/lint gates through the Builder workflow.
required_outputs: knowledge-ingestor grants owlbear-browser/browser_status beside its existing acquire grant and states that readiness/latest status is diagnostic only, not ingestion permission or authenticated-content proof.
A focused assertion in the maintained agent ecosystem suite couples the required caller grant to the registered browser_status tool without expanding interactive browser grants.
tasks.result: knowledge-ingestor can query Browser readiness beside acquire and is constrained to use it for diagnosis/routing, with live registry and agent-contract validation.
tasks.title: Grant diagnostic status to the maintained ingestion caller

acceptance_observations: AC-015: Given a fresh setup installation, tests/test_setup_init_settings.py observes the Browser MCP command/template mapping with mode and profile overrides absent; guide examples select macOS managed Edge by omission and preserve explicit Chromium/non-macOS setup.

AC-016: Given the updated Browser READMEs and setup guide, artifact inspection finds the seven-field status contract, four bounded startup reasons, one-workspace profile restriction, direct visible onboarding, and Chromium override with no extension-derived or universal authentication claim; relative links resolve.

AC-017: Given the assembled reviewed candidate on a managed Mac with stable Edge, the pilot starts the normal Browser MCP lifespan and confirms its visible owned Edge page plus ready browser_status; the operator opens approved SharePoint and Jira targets directly and confirms authenticated content for each target without an interactive MCP operation.

AC-018: Given that pilot session, normal shutdown and restart with the same OwlBear profile retain operator-confirmed session availability for the approved targets, emit no rejected --no-sandbox warning, and close only OwlBear-owned resources while the daily browser remains untouched.

AC-019: Given the completed pilot, bounded host/status/title observations and operator confirmations identify the reviewed commit and before/after restart results without retaining page content or session files; launcher/page evidence is explicitly separate from B2 acquisition classification.

AC-020: Given the completed chain at the reviewed candidate, the focused Browser, MCP lifecycle/status, agent-registry, and setup tests plus the maintained changed-path route complete with positive assertions, preserving #234 cleanup coverage; missing prerequisites or skipped required observations remain unverified.
constraints: Primary concern: setup/documentation and its acceptance procedure; do not edit setup/init.py because its existing template mechanism suffices.
Use one canonical status/configuration description with relative links; replace extension-implies-SSO wording and Chromium-only macOS setup advice without unrelated documentation cleanup.
Preserve the current domain-allowlist policy and do not add a dependency, package, profile override, or platform-forcing seed value.

Pilot targets require approved managed-device/operator access. Credentials, consent, site trust, and MFA stay in the visible lifespan-owned window; do not request or retain cookies, tokens, storage state, profile copies, page bodies, or session files.

The pilot is a required acceptance gate, not optional documentation. If the managed device/operator/approved targets are unavailable, Builder must use its bounded external-action blocking procedure and must not report the task or pilot complete.
Bind deterministic and pilot evidence to the reviewed candidate through the normal Builder/Finalizer workflow; no new proof-record schema or cleanup mechanism.
exclusions: Claims that the pilot proves universal authentication, automated ingestion readiness, delayed-page classification, or B2 final-article detection
CDP or daily-browser control; B5 interactive tools; setup engine redesign
Persisted sensitive pilot content or session state in repository/Delivery evidence
maintained_surfaces: seed/.vscode/mcp.json (maintain cross-platform default omission; edit only if parity requires it)
proof_boundaries: Run uv run pytest tests/test_setup_init_settings.py -q --tb=short and inspect its produced temporary MCP configuration; source/template inspection alone does not prove setup output.

At the reviewed worktree run uv run test serve/browser/src/owlbear_browser/playwright_launcher.py serve/browser-mcp/src/owlbear_browser_mcp/server.py tests/test_agent_ecosystem_validation.py tests/test_setup_init_settings.py plus uv run test --changed; use normal Builder-scoped lint gates for changed Python, Markdown, YAML frontmatter and JSON.

Execute the documented managed-device procedure through normal Browser MCP startup and its owned visible page; observe approved target identity, bounded status/title, operator-confirmed authenticated content, successful restart, no rejected sandbox warning, and owned-only cleanup. An exit code or deterministic fake is not a substitute for this gate.
required_outputs: Updated Browser and Browser MCP READMEs plus setup Browser-readiness guidance covering platform defaults, explicit Chromium, fixed managed profile, safe failure reasons/status, direct visible onboarding, single-workspace profile ownership, and bounded claims.

Seed/setup parity validation: keep BROWSER_MODE and PLAYWRIGHT_USER_DATA_DIR omitted in the cross-platform default seed, preserve the existing unrelated allowlist setting, and verify setup output against that template through tests/test_setup_init_settings.py; no seed byte change is required if its existing mapping remains suitable.

One maintained managed-Mac pilot procedure in setup/setup-guide.md, linked from the Browser MCP guide instead of duplicated; exact-candidate pilot observations for approved SharePoint and Jira hosts, direct operator authentication, restart persistence, sandbox warning absence, and owned-resource shutdown.
Focused and routed regression proof tied to the reviewed candidate; pilot observations are retained only as bounded Delivery proof, never page content or session files.
